source: W3C ODRL CG formal-semantics examples B1 (B11, B12)
notes: Translated from the W3C ODRL CG formal-semantics examples (w3c/odrl@1db8e6b, folder B Evaluation of Refinements/B1). The CG's evaluatedAction/Target/Party become the request; requestParameters describing sotw:CurrentXSDDateTime become request.at and effective_at (odrl:dateTime is the action time in due2-core). The CG reports a controlState: Inactive is Deny under its default 'close' behaviour, where due2 says NotApplicable and leaves the default to the enforcement point. Timezone-less instants are read as UTC (due2 instants are UTC, workflows §2). The CG request carries the resolution as a request parameter whose describesFeature is the unit IRI (Dots_per_inch) and whose value is written {"@id": "1000"} — an IRI, not an integer literal. Both are upstream defects; the translation reads them as the integer value of odrl:resolution. Upstream inconsistency: B12 reports the rule Active with an unsatisfied refinement and controlState Deny, where A12 reports an unsatisfied constraint as Inactive. In due2 a refinement is a constraint of scope action (workflows §3.1), so an F refinement means the atom does not apply, exactly like an F constraint.

expected.why: 1000 ≤ 1200, so the action refinement holds and ex:rule/B1 applies.
1300 > 1200: the refinement is F, so the atom does not apply (due2 does not distinguish a failed refinement from a failed constraint).

With no request param the operand is missing, so the refinement is U and the only candidate is uncertain: Permit or NotApplicable by completion, hence Indeterminate. The CG's closed behaviour would deny.
